message: No detected untrusted source handling: The DVC pull from a remote source has no checksum verification, signed URL, or authentication check beyond a non-zero exit code check.
No detected label flipping detection: No label distribution comparison, expected-set validation, or label-noise detection tool (e.g., Cleanlab) is present anywhere in the data preparation code.

No detected data poisoning defenses: The process_data function applies only encoding transformations with no outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or suspicious-input filtering on training samples.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads model.pkl, encoder.pkl, and labeler.pkl using pickle.load() with no hash check, signature verification, or pinned revision — just a plain file path with no integrity validation.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, expected label sets, or anomalous sample distribution before or during training.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no trigger detection, activation analysis, or gradient anomaly detection present in the training pipeline.
No detected differential privacy: The model is trained using sklearn's RandomForestClassifier with GridSearchCV and no differential privacy library or mechanism is used.

No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing frameworks (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD, etc.) are used anywhere in the code; evaluation only computes precision, recall, and F-beta on standard slices.

No detected metric tampering protection: There is no explicit isolation of a held-out test set from training data, no hashing or signing of evaluation data, and no mechanism to prevent metric manipulation; evaluation simply calls compute_model_metrics on whatever data is passed in.
No detected output bounds checks: The inference result is cast directly to int and returned with no NaN checks, probability bounds validation, or sanity checks on the model output.
No detected prompt injection defenses: This is a tabular ML model (RandomForestClassifier), not an LLM, so prompt injection defenses are not applicable and none are implemented.
